slides.teacher_cue: New sound. Tongue tip touches the ridge behind the upper teeth — like /t/ — then releases with friction — like /ʃ/. A combination of stop and fricative. Voice on. ch! ch! ch! Contrast with /ʃ/: sh is smooth — ch has a hard onset. Korean has a similar affricate ㅊ so production is accessible.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /tʃ/ cleanly as a voiced postalveolar affricate with a clear stop onset.
slides.correction_move: Model the contrast: /ʃ/ — smooth continuous friction. /tʃ/ — hard stop then friction. Students alternate sh-ch-sh-ch.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /ʃ/ substitution — the most likely error. Redirect: the ch has to start with a stop.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the new focus, then connect ch to one strong word from today.

slides.correction_move: Model the focus once, then have students echo and use it in a known word.
slides.observation_note: Listen for whether students can carry the focus from isolation into a real word.
